motions.motion_text:
BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Chair of the Board of Health Verbal Report, the Medical Officer of Health Verbal Report, and the reports titled: Renewal of Ottawa Public Health’s approach to Supporting Older Adults in Ottawa to Age Well, Risk Management at Ottawa Public Health and Attendance at the Association of Local Public Health Agencies’ (alPHa) Fall Symposium be received and considered;
AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the that the Rules of Procedure be suspended to receive and table the report titled “2026 Draft Operating Budget for the Ottawa Board of Health”.

sub_agendas_items.title: Chair of the Board of Health Verbal Report
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
The Chair welcomed attendees and introduced the 2026 Draft Operating Budget, noting it is the first step in the annual process and emphasizing the need for fair provincial funding to sustain services and meet growing health needs. The Chair reiterated that tonight’s meeting is for introduction and consultation, with full discussion and voting scheduled for December. The report acknowledged City Council’s recent motion on food insecurity and reaffirmed the Board’s commitment to addressing its root causes. The Chair highlighted Ottawa Public Health’s endorsement of the 2025 Position Statement on Active Outdoor Play and called for formal Board support. Finally, the Chair noted Dr. Arnason’s new biweekly media segment aimed at improving health literacy and countering misinformation.
Discussion of the item lasted approximately 8 minutes and no questions were received from the board on the topics discussed.

motions.motion_text: That the Board of Health for the City of Ottawa Health Unit receive this verbal report for information.

sub_agendas_items.title: Medical Officer of Health Verbal Report
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
The Medical Officer of Health reported on the closure of Ottawa Public Health’s supervised consumption and drug checking services at Clarence Street due to the expiry of federal exemption and lack of provincial approval, noting continued harm reduction and outreach services remain in place.
He confirmed the end of Ontario’s measles outbreak while cautioning about imported cases and emphasized maintaining high vaccination coverage.
Updates were provided on wastewater surveillance for COVID-19, flu, and RSV, which will continue through 2026, and on the availability of seasonal vaccines.
The report also highlighted preparations for implementing revised Ontario Public Health Standards in January 2026 and introduced the 2026 Draft Operating Budget. The MOH acknowledged staff and partners for their dedication and stressed the importance of evidence-based, collaborative approaches to address complex public health challenges.
Dr. Arnason took questions from Board Members. Discussion on the item lasted approximately 12 minutes.

motions.motion_text: That the Board of Health for the City of Ottawa Health Unit receive this verbal report for information.

sub_agendas_items.title: 2026 Draft Operating Budget for the Ottawa Board of Health

attachments.attachment_title: DOCUMENT 1 – 2026 Draft Operating Budget for the Ottawa Board of Health_EN.pdf
DOCUMENT 1 – Budget provisoire de fonctionnement pour 2026 pour le Conseil de santé d’Ottawa_FR.pdf

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Kibria Mohammad presented the 2026 Draft Operating Budget to the Board, accompanied by a PowerPoint presentation. Board members asked questions regarding electronic systems used in public health and their integration with hospital-based systems, as well as OPH’s approach to electronic records retention. Discussion also focused on provincial funding assumptions and contingency plans should anticipated funding does not materialize. The Board emphasized the importance of addressing the funding shortfall with the Province.
Discussion on this item lasted approximately 30 minutes.

motions.motion_text: That, at its meeting of November 3, 2025, the Board of Health for the City of Ottawa Health Unit:

sub_agendas_items.title: Renewal of Ottawa Public Health’s approach to Supporting Older Adults in Ottawa to Age Well

attachments.attachment_title: Renewal of Ottawa Public Health’s approach to Supporting Older Adults in Ottawa to Age Well.pdf

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Kelly Biggs and Erinn Salewski delivered a PowerPoint presentation to the Board outlining the renewed Older Adults Plan.
Board members expressed appreciation for staff collaboration with the City and asked questions about what distinguishes this plan, how its impact will be measured, and what success indicators will be used. Discussion included plans for rural areas, opportunities to partner with organizations such as the Heart Institute and initiatives like the “Mole-Mobile.” Members also inquired about consultation with groups advocating for adults with different abilities, noting the need for health promotion activities alongside disease prevention. Staff indicated that while direct work has not yet occurred, collaboration with colleagues in Community and Social Services is possible, and current efforts include using Neighborhood Health and Wellness Hubs for promotion activities. Strength and balance programming was highlighted as a priority, given that falls remain a leading cause of hospitalization among older adults.
The Board also heard from two delegations: Community and Social Services Department and Age-Friendly Ottawa.
Discussion on this item lasted approximately 45 minutes.

motions.motion_text: That the Board of Health for the City of Ottawa:

sub_agendas_items.title: Risk Management at Ottawa Public Health

attachments.attachment_title: 7.5 Risk Management at Ottawa Public Health.pdf

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Dr. Trevor Arnason provided a brief comment emphasizing the report as a key component of Ottawa Public Health’s accountability to the Board and the Ministry of Health. He noted that the report outlines strategies to mitigate major risks such as climate change, technological challenges, and increasing complexity of community health needs amid stagnant provincial funding, and reaffirmed OPH’s commitment to proactive risk management and ongoing reporting.
Dr. Arnason and Cameron Keyes responded to questions from Board members.
Discussion on this item lasted approximately four minutes.

motions.motion_text: That the Board of Health for the City of Ottawa Health Unit receive this report for information.
